clue.text: Finding excuse to dash off and book exhumation

parts.note: digging a buried body back up is undoing a burial

explanation.surface: Someone invents a pretext to rush away and reserve a place at a disinterment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, where Algernon invents an invalid friend, Bunbury, as an excuse to leave town.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wilde's play, inventing a fictitious friend to escape social duties is called by this name, so it means contriving an excuse to slip away.

clue.text: Bruce Forsyth repeatedly says '1, 2, 3, 4' and dances

indicators.note: 1 asks for the first letter of the first word
2 asks for the second letter of the second word
3 asks for the third letter of the third word
4 asks for the fourth letter of the fourth word

explanation.surface: The TV host Bruce Forsyth keeps counting dancers in on Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce Forsyth hosted the BBC ballroom show Strictly Come Dancing. The numbers tell you which letter of each successive word to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is to dance informally to pop music, so the plural verb matches dances.

clue.text: Persons or person stupidly rejecting proportional representation?

indicators.note: stupidly means foolishly, so the remaining letters are jumbled
rejecting means casting out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the word taken as written

explanation.surface: A topical jibe at people who foolishly vote against voting reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes PR out of PERSON, and 'stupidly' rearranges ESON. The clue appeared just before Britain's 2011 referendum on changing the voting system.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who vote against a motion in Parliament are counted as this plural, so it names persons voting no.

clue.text: Singular noun I query, defining it more narrowly

indicators.note: narrowing the definition of the phrase trims letters off both ends, leaving a run from inside it

explanation.surface: A grammarian queries a noun to pin down its meaning more precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'noun I query' once the outer letters are trimmed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one of a kind, without equal, is what singular means in its sense of remarkable or unparalleled.

clue.text: Possibly play song with bounce relevantly somehow passing on G.B.S.

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
letters to remove, taken as written
the initials of George Bernard Shaw, taken as letters without the dots

explanation.surface: A tune with relevant pep is handed on to George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing on' means discarding: those two letters and Shaw's initials leave the pool, and the anagram signal rearranges what is left. The answer is an 1897 Shaw comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1897 comedy by George Bernard Shaw is an example of a play, hence 'Possibly'.

clue.text: Look in nursery nurses' cases for stockings

indicators.note: in places the exclamation inside the outer letters
the cases of words are their outside letters

parts.note: LO is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Check inside the bags of the nursery nurses for hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' takes N...Y and N...S from 'nursery nurses''; LO goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's stockings were made from this synthetic fibre, so the word became a common name for them.

clue.text: Spin as some bowling may be if not so

indicators.note: to spin the letters is to whirl them round into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
the word to be removed from the fodder before rearranging, signalled by if not

explanation.surface: A cricket remark: bowling might be spin, or if not that, something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: AS SOME with the letters of SO taken away ('if not so') leaves A, M, E, S to rearrange. 'Spin' reads as the cricket type, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowling is broadly either spin or the faster style that uses the ball's stitching to make it deviate off the pitch.

clue.text: Flicks each X-rated with Rome's authority

indicators.note: a flick jolts things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Every film is restricted to adults by order of the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flicks' looks like films alongside 'X-rated'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means from the chair, used of papal pronouncements made with full official authority.

clue.text: Male peripatetic teachers covering new city

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
peripatetic means wandering about, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man among travelling teachers who cover a new town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripatetic' rearranges TEACHERS and 'covering' wraps them round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in north-west England, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Before your lips curled masking suspicions of extortion and vice

indicators.note: masking means covering up, so the rearranged letters wrap round the other pair
curled lips are twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: a suspicion of something is a faint trace of it, so just the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A sneer conceals a hint that someone suspects blackmail and wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curled' rearranges YOUR LIPS; 'suspicions of' takes E and V from 'extortion and vice'; 'masking' puts EV inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier or at a prior time is a plain synonym for before, used as an adverb.

clue.text: Use tomography for cases in Sweden and Norway. It's characteristic of them

indicators.note: in tells us the cases go inside the letters for the two countries

parts.note: S is the international vehicle registration code for Sweden
N is the international vehicle registration code for Norway
CA is the abbreviation for case, as in law reports; here plural cases

explanation.surface: A medical note about using imaging on patients in Scandinavia, adding that it is typical of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The final sentence is an extra nod: the answer is also a short form of Scandinavian, so it is 'characteristic' of Swedes and Norwegians. It adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomography builds cross-sectional images of the body, so using it on someone is subjecting them to an imaging examination.

clue.text: But for joke miss out television for instance and 'to boldly go'

definitions.text: television for instance and 'to boldly go'

parts.note: bar means except, so but for
BAR is a Scots word for a joke

indicators.note: out means awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Apart from a gag, omit the TV and Star Trek's famous split infinitive.
explanation.walkthrough: Television mixes Greek and Latin roots, and 'to boldly go' splits an infinitive: purists condemn both.
explanation.definitionFit: Language purists label such mongrel words and grammatical lapses as crude misuses of the language.

clue.text: True to a person of outstanding virtue. The Queen!

parts.note: loyal means true or faithful
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A declaration of fidelity to a paragon, ending with a raised glass to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: At British formal dinners the first drink is to the monarch, proposed with the words 'The Queen!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The words spoken when proposing the formal drink to the sovereign at a dinner, so they stand for that toast.

clue.text: Beastly clue about gobbling northern cattle feed

indicators.note: beastly means nasty or misbehaving, so the word clue is mangled into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A solver complains about a horrid clue that seems to devour a northern word for fodder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests cattle, matching the feed, but it only signals the rearrangement; 'gobbling' then puts northern inside the word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant is alfalfa, a leguminous crop grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Academician in Berlin edited ancient Greek script

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
edited means revised, so the city's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
A is the abbreviation for academician

explanation.surface: A scholar in Germany's capital revised an ancient script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges BERLIN to LINER B; A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mycenaean syllabic writing deciphered by Michael Ventris records an early form of the Greek language.

clue.text: In charge in Eden wrongly eating fruit finally if tempted

indicators.note: in, with eating, says the following letters go inside the rearranged garden name
eating means taking inside, so the rearranged letters swallow the other pieces
wrongly signals the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of fruit

explanation.surface: In Eden, someone wrongly ate fruit and was thereby led astray, as in Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the garden's name to ENED, which takes the fruit's last letter and the charge abbreviation into its middle. The Genesis surface makes 'tempted' feel like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Lured or persuaded by temptation, so it is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: A refusal leads to murmurs, insults and eventually breakdown in civilised conduct

parts.note: saying no is a refusal

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A rejection escalates into mutterings, abuse and finally a collapse of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes M, I and E from 'murmurs, insults and eventually'; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociologists use this term, from Durkheim, for a state where social norms and standards have collapsed.

clue.text: Telltale tingle: half of that first sounds like 2

indicators.note: first places the tin symbol at the front

parts.note: that points back to tingle, whose first half, tin, has the chemical symbol SN
a tingle is an itch

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction about a tingling sensation that sounds like another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of 'tingle' is TIN, which becomes its chemical symbol. 'sounds like 2' is a second hint: 2 Down sounds like 'nose', slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale is someone who informs on others, and the slang word for such a sneak is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Guilt for a sin the Wombles rule out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The Wombles, the litter-collecting children's TV creatures, decree something sinful forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are furry creatures from a British children's TV show who tidy Wimbledon Common. 'out' rearranges A SIN THE WOMBLES plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving censure or culpability is the state of being guilty, so this abstract noun matches guilt.

clue.text: Sharp answer rebuffed revolutionary sign of hesitation

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: TROT is short for Trotskyist, a revolutionary
ER is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A cutting reply put down a radical's hesitant mumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns TROTER round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, witty or cutting reply is the standard meaning of this word as a noun.

clue.text: Tie? With Thailand there may be

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

indicators.note: may be signals the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether there might be a necktie in Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or chain that ties an animal to a post, and as a verb to tie up; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Pilot organization in move to the right

indicators.note: in tells us the organisation sits inside the horse command

parts.note: GEE is a call to a horse to turn right
ORG is short for organization

explanation.surface: A pilot organisation moves to the right, perhaps politically.
explanation.walkthrough: In airmen's slang this name is the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang name for the automatic pilot that flies the plane, so it fits pilot as a crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Tiered seats require some back protection I'd argue

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone argues that tiered seating needs some back support.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'require', but that word is a link joining definition to wordplay; a tier of seats is the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a step or tier of seats, as in an amphitheatre, so it describes tiered seating.

clue.text: Service held by brave French abbot

indicators.note: held by means enclosed within the other piece

parts.note: to beard is to brave or defy someone
RN, the Royal Navy, is the Senior Service

explanation.surface: A church service is conducted by a courageous French abbot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is RN, the Royal Navy, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Bernard of Clairvaux was the famous French Cistercian abbot of the twelfth century.

clue.text: Earliest signs of spud harvest and wood

definitions.text: Earliest signs of spud harvest and wood

indicators.note: the earliest sign of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The first indications of a potato crop, and of a copse.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Scots for the stalks and leaves of potatoes, which show before harvest, and also an old word for a small wood: the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the haulm of a potato plant goes by this name, and in older English it means a thicket or small wood.

clue.text: Graduate at British university may be superficially learned

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: someone who is only superficially educated

parts.note: BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate from a British university may have only a thin education.
explanation.walkthrough: In British India the term, once a title like Mr, came to mean a clerk with a smattering of English education.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian use it was a slighting term for an Indian clerk thought to have only a veneer of English learning.

clue.text: Scots very ruthless with iron will

parts.note: FE is the chemical symbol for iron
LL is the contracted form of will, as in I'll

explanation.surface: A Scottish character is extremely ruthless, with a will of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots very' is a second hint: in Scots the word also means very or extremely.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old literary adjective it means fierce or cruel, as in the phrase 'one fell swoop'.

clue.text: Trite postings on one topic are located by browser first

parts.note: a thread is a chain of online messages on one subject

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of browser

explanation.surface: Online forum chatter on one subject is dull, as a web browser finds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'located by' is a link: the browser's first letter sits beside ARE, given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn thin with overuse, an argument or joke can be hackneyed, which is the figurative sense of trite.

clue.text: Widow for a short time in south India's capital?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the capital of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A widow is visiting southern India's capital briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the word names the old Hindu practice of a widow burning herself on her husband's pyre, also applied to the widow herself; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is used for a Hindu widow who immolated herself on her husband's funeral pyre.

clue.text: Squeeze girl up lane before anything's said

indicators.note: squeezing deforms the shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man hugs his girlfriend up a lane before a word is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' looks like a girlfriend or a hug; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the stage before a child acquires speech, so it means preceding the use of language.
